content: Artemisia afra is a widely distributed species of the Artemisia genus in Africa, ranging from South Africa to regions in the north and east, extending as far as Ethiopia. It is the only species of this genus that is indigenous to the African continent. The plant grows in dense clumps, with woody, ridged stems that can reach heights between 0.5 meters and 2 meters. Its leaves are dark green, soft in texture, and resemble the shape of fern leaves. The undersides of the leaves are lighter green and covered with fine white bristles. During late summer, Artemisia afra produces numerous small, butter-colored flowers, each measuring approximately 3 to 5 millimeters in diameter. When any part of the plant is crushed or bruised, it emits a strong, sweet, and pungent aroma. Artemisia afra is a prominent medicinal plant in Africa and continues to be used effectively across various cultures. Its applications include the treatment of respiratory conditions such as coughs, fevers, and colic, as well as headaches, intestinal parasites, and malaria. Beyond its medicinal uses, the plant is also employed as a natural moth repellent and as an ingredient in organic insecticidal sprays. Different parts of the plant, including the roots, stems, and leaves, are utilized in various forms such as enemas, poultices, infusions, lotions, or through inhalation (e.g., smoking or snuffing). Additionally, it is processed into essential oil for therapeutic purposes. The essential oil of Artemisia afra is extracted through steam distillation of its twigs and blossoms. Chemical analysis using gas chromatography reveals that the oil contains several bioactive compounds characteristic of the Artemisia genus. The primary components include α-thujone (52.9%), β-thujone (15.07%), and 1,8-cineole (10.66%). Other notable constituents are camphor (5.72%), germacrene (1.60%), δ-cadinene (1.16%), α-terpineol (0.96%), e-chrysanthenyl acetate (0.78%), camphene (0.71%), β-pinene (0.51%), α-pinene (0.46%), trans-β-ocimene (0.45%), and myrcene (0.22%). These compounds contribute to the plant's medicinal properties and aromatic profile.
